cards.front: Define the Internet of Things (IoT).
cards.back: A network of physical objects embedded with **sensors, software, and connectivity** that let them **collect, exchange, and act on data** with little/no human intervention — 'a world where things talk.'

cards.front: The four core concepts (pillars) of IoT?
cards.back: **Connectivity** (reach the internet), **Sensing** (capture the world), **Communication** (MQTT/CoAP/HTTP), **Analytics** (data → decisions).

cards.front: What four capabilities make an object 'smart'?
cards.back: **Sensing** (sensors) + **Actuation** (actuators) + **Processing** (microcontroller) + **Communication** (radio/network).

cards.front: Who coined 'Internet of Things', when, and why?
cards.back: **Kevin Ashton**, **1999**, at MIT's **Auto-ID Center** — for **RFID-based supply-chain tracking** (letting objects gather their own data instead of humans typing it).

cards.front: First internet-connected appliance (often cited)?
cards.back: The early-1980s **Carnegie Mellon Coke machine**, wired to ARPANET to check stock and bottle temperature remotely.

cards.front: IoT traffic vs human traffic — the key inversion?
cards.back: Humans = **downlink-heavy**, bursty, daytime peaks (consumers). IoT = **uplink-heavy**, event-based/periodic, mostly stationary (producers).

cards.front: Why can a tiny smart-meter outage alert outrank megabytes of routine data?
cards.back: Importance = **latency + reliability**, not volume. A few-byte outage alert is urgent; routine telemetry can be best-effort.

cards.front: The 'iron triangle' of IoT connectivity?
cards.back: **Range ↔ Power ↔ Data-rate** — you usually get two of {long range, low power, high data rate}, never all three.

cards.front: What is an LPWAN? Give examples.
cards.back: **Low-Power Wide-Area Network** — long range + very low power at low data rates. Examples: **LoRaWAN, NB-IoT, Sigfox**.

cards.front: What is an IoT gateway and why is it needed?
cards.back: A bridge between local (short-range/non-IP) devices and the cloud. Needed for **protocol translation, aggregation, edge processing, security, bridging, device management**.

cards.front: Gateway: 'converts BLE/Zigbee data into HTTP/MQTT/CoAP' is which function?
cards.back: **Protocol translation** (vs aggregation = combine many devices; bridging = non-IP↔IP networks).

cards.front: Digitization vs digital transformation?
cards.back: **Digitization** = converting analog info/processes to digital. **Digital transformation** = the broader business change it enables (new models, predictive maintenance).

cards.front: What data type do most IoT devices produce, and why does it suit AI?
cards.back: **Time-series** (timestamped, repeatedly sampled) — the native shape of the physical world; ideal for forecasting, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance.

cards.front: Horizontal platform vs IoT vertical?
cards.back: **Horizontal** = cross-industry foundation (cloud, analytics, security). **Vertical** = industry-specific end-use domain (healthcare, manufacturing) where impact is created.

cards.front: IIoT is the backbone of what, and its 3 flagship use cases?
cards.back: Backbone of **Industry 4.0**. Flagships: **predictive maintenance, asset tracking/uptime, digital-twin modelling**.

cards.front: Reactive vs preventive vs predictive maintenance?
cards.back: **Reactive** = fix after failure (downtime). **Preventive** = fix on a calendar (too early/late). **Predictive** = fix exactly when sensor data says — the cost sweet spot.

cards.front: Smart-city key components?
cards.back: **Smart governance** (data-driven planning), **smart mobility/traffic** (adaptive signals, smart parking), **smart environment** (pollution, water/waste, disaster sensors).

cards.front: IoMT and RPM?
cards.back: **IoMT** = Internet of Medical Things. **RPM** = Remote Patient Monitoring — wearables stream vitals (HR, SpO₂, glucose) to providers for early intervention.

cards.front: The 4-step smart-farming loop?
cards.back: **Data collection → Diagnostics → Decision-making → Action** (then re-measure and repeat).

cards.front: V2X, V2V, V2I?
cards.back: **V2X** = vehicle-to-everything; includes **V2V** (vehicle-to-vehicle) and **V2I** (vehicle-to-infrastructure) — lets cars 'see around corners.'

cards.front: Name the major IoT challenges.
cards.back: Security & privacy, interoperability/standards, connectivity/reliability, power management, data overload, scalability, high initial cost.

cards.front: What was the Mirai (2016) attack, and which challenge does it show?
cards.back: IoT devices with **default credentials** hijacked into a **DDoS botnet** — the classic **security & privacy** challenge (weakest endpoint endangers all).

cards.front: The core power-management trade-off for sensors?
cards.back: **Transmission frequency vs battery life** — each transmission drains power, so devices batch and sleep, trading data freshness for years of life.

cards.front: What is an IoT 'architectural driver'?
cards.back: A **force/goal/constraint** (technical, economic, user) that shapes the architecture — not a physical component. E.g., low latency → edge computing.

cards.front: Horizontal vs vertical scaling?
cards.back: **Horizontal** = add more nodes (scale **out**). **Vertical** = make one machine bigger (scale **up**). IoT favours horizontal.

cards.front: Four types of latency in IoT?
cards.back: **Network** (travel), **processing** (analysis), **actuation** (command→action), **end-to-end** (event→completed action).

cards.front: Which driver most directly forces edge computing?
cards.back: **Latency / real-time response** — a cloud round-trip is too slow when milliseconds decide safety, so processing moves to the edge.

cards.front: The 3-layer IoT architecture?
cards.back: **Perception** (sensors/RFID — sense) → **Network** (transport) → **Application** (user services). Mnemonic: sense → move → use.

cards.front: What does the 5-layer model add over the 3-layer?
cards.back: Inserts a **Data-Processing/middleware ('brain')** layer and a **Service/Business** layer for finer separation of analytics and business logic.

cards.front: Cloud-centric vs edge/fog-centric architecture trade-off?
cards.back: **Cloud** = scale + heavy analytics, but round-trip latency. **Edge/fog** = low latency, bandwidth-thrifty, offline-resilient. Most systems are **hybrid**.

cards.front: What is a digital twin?
cards.back: A continuously-updated **virtual replica** of a physical asset (fed by its live data) for **simulation, monitoring, and predictive maintenance** — risk-free testing on the copy.

cards.front: AIoT?
cards.back: **AI + IoT** — embedding ML (edge or cloud, incl. TinyML) so devices predict, classify, and learn; the architectural form of the 'intelligence' driver.

cards.front: oneM2M's three core entities?
cards.back: **AE** (Application Entity — app logic), **CSE** (Common Services Entity — the core service layer), **NSE** (Network Services Entity — telecom interface).

cards.front: Where is the CSE deployed (its node types)?
cards.back: **IN-CSE** (cloud/data centre), **MN-CSE** (gateway/fog/edge), **application/device node** (on the device). Same services at each tier → interoperability.

cards.front: What is the IoTWF model and who proposed it?
cards.back: A **7-layer reference model** by **Cisco** (IoT World Forum) for industrial IoT, with **security & management spanning all layers** (cross-cutting).

cards.front: Name the canonical Cisco IoTWF 7 layers (bottom→top).
cards.back: 1 Physical Devices & Controllers → 2 Connectivity → 3 Edge/Fog Computing → 4 Data Accumulation → 5 Data Abstraction → 6 Application → 7 Collaboration & Processes.

cards.front: The three layers of the Core IoT Functional Stack?
cards.back: **Things** (sensors/actuators), **Communications Network** (transfers data), **Applications & Analytics** (use data + decide).

cards.front: Four sublayers of the Communications Network layer?
cards.back: **Access network** (last hop to device), **Gateways & backhaul** (aggregate), **Network transport** (IP/UDP), **IoT network management** (CoAP/MQTT).

cards.front: Edge vs fog vs cloud — one line each.
cards.back: **Edge** = on/near device, ultra-low latency, autonomous reflexes. **Fog** = LAN-level, aggregates a site. **Cloud** = remote, massive scale + heavy AI/ML + long-term storage.

cards.front: Why does pushing compute to the edge help?
cards.back: Cuts **latency** (no cloud round-trip), saves **bandwidth** (send only relevant data), and gives **autonomy** (works during network disruption).

cards.front: The IoT value chain stages?
cards.back: **Silicon/hardware → devices → connectivity → IoT platform → analytics/apps → end service.** Value/margin concentrates toward the **service** end.

cards.front: Match standards bodies to their IoT role.
cards.back: **IEEE** (Wi-Fi/802.15.4 radios), **IETF** (CoAP/6LoWPAN), **3GPP** (NB-IoT/LTE-M/5G), **oneM2M** (service layer), **ISO/IEC 30141** (reference architecture).
